name: Absolutism
summary: Absolutism holds that sovereign power should rest wholly in a monarch, unrestrained by legislatures, churches or social elites. It is justified by divine right and by the theory that sovereignty is indivisible and perpetual, though classic theorists still bind the ruler to natural and divine law. In practice it centralised law, built standing armies and bureaucracies, subordinated the church and favoured mercantilist economics.
scope: Classical European absolutism of roughly 1600 to 1789, based on Jean Bodin on sovereignty, James VI and I, Bossuet and the court of Louis XIV. Excludes later enlightened absolutism and modern dictatorships, and many answers on modern issues are inferred.

keyFigures.name: Jean Bodin
keyFigures.role: French jurist who formulated the theory of absolute, indivisible sovereignty.

keyFigures.name: Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet
keyFigures.role: Bishop who set out divine-right monarchy for Louis XIV's court.

keyFigures.name: James VI and I
keyFigures.role: King who argued for royal supremacy over law and parliament in The True Law of Free Monarchies.

sources.usedFor: King as author of law, parliament subordinate, power over life and death, welfare as chief law.

universal-healthcare.rationale: No doctrine on healthcare; a paternal crown could fund hospitals, but nothing in the sources commits it either way.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage-setting was a matter of crown and guild regulation, but there is no documented stance on raising pay for workers' sake.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Absolutist governments generally pursued mercantilism, with the crown steering trade and production rather than trusting free prices.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred from mercantilist state direction, royal monopolies and crown-run enterprises; not a stated principle.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The crown wanted revenue from those most able to pay but struggled to tax privileged elites; no principled stance on soaking the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: independent associations with their own power sit badly with a ruler unrestrained by other institutions; guilds were crown-licensed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bodin protects property as bounded by natural law yet the sovereign remains supreme over subjects, so adherents differ on how hard it is to override.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from mercantilist regulation of trade and guilds by the crown.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: a paternal ruler owes care to subjects, so cutting aid as dependency-forming is not a natural absolutist line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: collective ownership by workers is foreign to a hierarchical order of estates under the king.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: a ruler answerable to no worldly body treats state security as overriding privacy; royal police and censorship were routine.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from a paternal, scripture-grounded state that regulates subjects' morals.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: attacks on the sacred order and on persons were punishable, and absolutist states censored freely; modern group-hate framing is anachronistic.

strong-leader.rationale: Absolutism is monarchical power unrestrained by legislatures, churches or elites, which is exactly a leader bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Bodin and Bossuet treat the state and sovereign power as necessary and divinely sanctioned.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: the crown monopolised force and disarmed independent power centres such as nobles.

empower-police-military.rationale: Professional standing armies and a bureaucracy dependent on the ruler were hallmarks of absolutist rule.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the scripture-based moral order Bossuet describes.

decide-locally.rationale: Absolutism consolidated power in the monarch and ended feudal partitioning, unifying law across the realm.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred: the king holds power of life and death and punishment is an exercise of sovereignty rather than reform.

traditional-family.rationale: Bossuet grounds royal power on paternal authority, so the family is the model of the political order.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the scripture-based Christian moral order.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from confessional Christian monarchy and Bodin's insistence on divine commandments.

more-religion-public.rationale: Bossuet says the service of God and respect for kings are bound together, and rulers rule by divine right.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the hierarchical order of privileged estates, with no programme of redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the paternal, scriptural order.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred: unified law, language and court culture were tools of consolidating the realm.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred: attacking established authority is sacrilege for Bossuet, though absolutism itself overrode feudal institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mercantilists wanted population and skills while confessional states expelled dissenters; no clear stance.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Bodin's sovereignty is absolute, indivisible and perpetual, leaving no room for a higher body.

free-trade.rationale: Absolutist governments generally pursued mercantilist economic policies.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from the sovereign's supremacy and dynastic pursuit of the state's strength.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: sovereignty is indivisible and rulers answer to God, not outside powers; the issue is anachronistic.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from indivisible sovereignty over a defined realm.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: mercantilist states sought wealth and population growth for state power.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; a strong ruler could act decisively but no documented position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Anachronistic; no documented position outside later enlightened absolutism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis for an answer.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bodin forbids killing even a cruel absolute sovereign and Bossuet calls attacks on the king sacrilege.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred: subjects had no political voice while a bureaucracy of royal officials administered policy.

central-planning.rationale: The crown directed trade under mercantilism, but a comprehensively planned economy is not an absolutist aim.

socialized-markets.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from mercantilist crown-directed rather than worker- or public-owned markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; no documented position and nobles' privileged land was a political constraint.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: the order of hereditary estates and dynastic inheritance underpins the system.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from paternal but not egalitarian cash entitlements.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Mercantilist policy of protecting and promoting domestic production was typical of absolutist governments.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Crown-sponsored manufactures and trading companies were standard mercantilist practice.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Bodin defends property of family and subjects but no programme of spreading ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Anachronistic; incompatible with the mercantilist, money-centred crown economy.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: crown-licensed guilds and orders under royal supervision resemble state-recognised bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Anachronistic; power rests in the monarch, not a party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Bossuet presents hereditary monarchy as natural, universal and divinely ordained.

democracy-best.rationale: Absolutist rulers generally gave subjects no political voice.

direct-votes.rationale: Subjects had no political voice and laws came from the sovereign.

workers-councils.rationale: Power was concentrated in the monarch, with no room for councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Sovereignty is indivisible and perpetual, so regions cannot detach.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rule is hereditary and divinely ordained, which implies some are fitted to rule by birth.

political-violence-never.rationale: Subjects' violence against the sovereign is never justified, but the state's own violence is, and Bodin allows tyrannicide against usurpers.

war-builds-character.rationale: Dynastic warfare was common but no documented doctrine on its character-building effect.

separate-church-state.rationale: Absolutism brought the church under state control and tied religion to the throne rather than separating them.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Bossuet derives politics from scripture and Bodin binds the sovereign to divine commandments.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The king is the source of law and holds justice and life-and-death power; privatising these contradicts sovereignty.

military-superiority.rationale: Standing armies and dynastic competition made military strength a core state aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Inferred: absolutist states were dynastic and multiethnic, with loyalty owed to the crown.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bossuet stresses paternal harmony under the king rather than conflict between classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The system rested on a hierarchy of estates with privileged nobility.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred: the king is origin of land titles, so authority flows from the crown.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from absolutist monarchies being colonial powers themselves.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from sovereignty over a particular realm.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred: Bossuet requires subjects to obey and the king to use power in fear of God.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Subjects' duty is obedience and individuals' only protection against authority is their innocence.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: mercantilists generally valued population as a source of state strength.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred: the system prized order and the king's authority over disruptive change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a scripture-based moral order.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; sovereignty rests in a person, not an algorithm.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred: a sovereign unchecked by other institutions would not accept communications beyond its reach.

restore-past-order.rationale: Adherents invoked tradition and divine order, yet absolutism itself overrode older feudal arrangements.

results-over-ideology.rationale: James says the commonwealth's welfare is the chief law, but divine right is doctrinal; genuinely split.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred from the sacred standing of the king and ban on resistance.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Anachronistic; incompatible with a developed state and court.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Anachronistic; the system rested on a hierarchy of orders and a specialised bureaucracy.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred from a hierarchical order with privilege by estate.

production-for-use.rationale: Anachronistic; mercantilist states sought wealth and revenue from production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a hierarchy that does not frame profit as exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anachronistic; power belongs to the monarch and the ruling order.

collective-farming.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from landed estates and peasant holdings under the crown.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anachronistic; the system predates mature capitalism and rejects the framing.

taxation-theft.rationale: Sovereign power includes taxation, though Bodin held subjects' consent mattered for subsidies; adherents reject calling it theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Bossuet ties the state to religion and morals, so restrictions go beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The order consisted of corporate estates and privileges, with subjects holding few political rights.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from standing armies and the ruler's command over subjects.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: subjects owe obedience to the sovereign, and states restricted emigration.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from a ruler holding a sacred trust rather than serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred; subjects were not understood as holders of a freedom claim.

organic-representation.rationale: Absolutism marginalised estates and gave subjects no political voice.

total-state.rationale: Bodin's sovereign remains bound by natural and divine law and scholars stress the gap between rhetoric and real power.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred: absolutism defends established dynastic order, not radical regeneration.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred from dynastic wars to extend a ruler's realm, such as those of Louis XIV.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Absolutism replaced feudal ties between lords and vassals with a bureaucracy dependent on the ruler.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom persisted in some absolutist states and was ended by enlightened rulers; split.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: Bossuet derives politics from scripture as truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Bodin binds even the sovereign to natural and divine law, which hold universally.

single-common-good.rationale: James treats the commonwealth's welfare as the king's chief law, not a balancing of group interests.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from hierarchical corporate order.

school-vouchers.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a state-church-linked education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Governments were chronically short of money but no doctrine on deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred: absolutist states steered the economy and gave no political freedom, so the claim is unfamiliar.

rule-by-example.rationale: Bossuet asks the king for fear and self-restraint, but the king remains lawmaker enforcing law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Dynastic sovereignty, not national will, defines the state.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred: a sovereign is not bound by any higher human authority in deciding war.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Bossuet argues from scripture rather than reason.

class-collaboration.rationale: Bossuet's paternal monarchy presents the king as above and harmonising the orders of society.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: Baroque courts and royal institutions celebrated inherited culture.

workers-nation.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis for a working-class politics.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the patriarchal, scriptural order.

ban-interest.rationale: Religious ban on usury existed but mercantilist states relied on credit; split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Anachronistic; the system distinguished estates and religion rather than race by law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Absolutists present the king as a paternal sovereign above classes, not an instrument of one.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Confessional states pressed religious conformity but no documented national-culture assimilation doctrine.

elite-replacement.rationale: Anachronistic conspiracy theory; no basis in the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred: subjects had no political voice, so representation by parties is irrelevant.

national-mission.rationale: No documented stance, though dynastic and religious missions occurred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents regard the paternal order as natural, not as systematic disadvantage.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Inferred: absolutists defended the king and his officials against estates and critics.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a Christian moral order.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred: no one may hold the sovereign to account by force and he answers to God alone.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Absolutist states directed economy, church and law, far beyond minimal functions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality before God is Christian, but the order rested on legally privileged estates.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from monarchies being colonial powers.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: States codified and unified law, replacing feudal and local variations.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Bodin sought religious concord under one faith and confessional monarchies restricted worship.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion and the throne are bound together, so religious instruction is normal.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Power rests on divine right with subjects given no political voice.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism, the usual absolutist economic policy, aimed at exporting more than importing.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from confessional policy such as expelling dissenters from the realm.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The sovereign holds power of life and death and wages war, so force is a sovereign prerogative.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred: Bossuet stresses charity and order under the king.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred: a sovereign suppresses movements seeking to overthrow the order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Absolutism is by definition power unrestrained by institutions, so subjects depend on the ruler's will, even if used with restraint.

separated-powers.rationale: Bodin holds sovereignty to be indivisible and James calls parliament the king's court.

vanguard-party.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from monarchy rather than a revolutionary party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Bossuet's kings answer to God for their rule and had Christian duties to the poor, but no priority is documented.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from a crown that curbs independent organisation and revolt.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Bodin sought religious concord, valuing unity of faith for order.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices depend on the ruler's appointment, with a bureaucracy answering solely to him.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred: the sovereign is not bound by positive law, only natural and divine law, and may act on necessity.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from paternal regulation of grain and markets by crown officials.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred: royal licensing and censorship; the party framing is anachronistic.

party-commands-army.rationale: Anachronistic; the king commands the army directly.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Anachronistic; no elected representatives in the doctrine.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Bodin's sovereignty is absolute, indivisible and perpetual and cannot be pooled.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The monarch commands the army and appoints ministers, with a bureaucracy dependent on the ruler.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred: Bossuet's Gallican Catholicism was episcopal and tied to the crown.

clerical-rule.rationale: Absolutism brought the church under state control and reduced its influence.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Disloyalty to the sovereign in war is a sacrilegious act against a divinely ordained ruler.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from a scripture-based moral order and royal censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: monarchs rule for life, so term limits are alien.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: officials answer to the ruler alone, not voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Dynastic alliances were common but no principled stance.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a property-and-estates order.

people-in-arms.rationale: Professional standing armies were a hallmark of absolutism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Dynastic claims, not national reunification, drive the doctrine.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from a Christian, hierarchical outlook.

death-penalty.rationale: James affirms the king's power over life and death and Bodin supports severe penalties.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from reliance on scripture.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from a state enforcing scripture-based morals.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Anachronistic; dynastic subjecthood has no stated rule.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from state unification of law and administration.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Bodin accepted tolerance only as a step to concord and the state, not minorities, determines worship.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from an order stressing obedience, tradition and religion.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anachronistic; rulers did repudiate debts but no doctrine.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making by an elected assembly contradicts sovereign power resting in the monarch.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred: mercantilist rulers pursued state wealth while giving subjects no political voice.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred: absolutist rulers sought independent military power.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rule is hereditary and divinely sanctioned, not elected.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Anachronistic; the crown's finance would not be independent of the sovereign.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: James makes the commonwealth's welfare the king's chief law, and the king originally distributed the land.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: dynastic claims and annexations were routine.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Absolutism brought the church under state control and reduced its power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: the king stands above factions as father of the nation, though he also governs.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Sovereignty is indivisible and perpetual, so the sovereign defends the realm's unity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: States codified and unified law and consolidated power, opposing local variation.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Bossuet calls the throne the throne of God and the king's person sacred, though divine descent is not claimed.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Bodin defines the absolute sovereign as free from civil law while bound by natural and divine law, and James calls kings the makers of the laws.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hereditary monarchy and a fixed social hierarchy, which treat station and royal blood as innate.

space-expansion.rationale: Absolutism predates space travel; the sources give no basis for either answer.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Bodin held sovereignty is indivisible and so cannot be shared between the few and the many; absolutism rests on one sovereign.

leader-cult.rationale: Bossuet presents royal majesty as sacred and the king as the image of God, and the court made public praise of the monarch central to rule.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the paternal model of authority in Bossuet and James VI and I, which gives the father headship of the family.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the hierarchical order of estates under a sovereign monarch, which leaves no place for class struggle against it.

land-redistribution.rationale: Bodin holds that the sovereign is bound by natural law, which includes respect for private property, so seizing estates for redistribution is ruled out.

refugee-return.rationale: No documented doctrine; the question belongs to a later era of nationalist conflicts, so adherents have no stated position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims rested on dynastic inheritance and treaty, not on the nationality of inhabitants; inferred from the dynastic character of absolute monarchy.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Absolutist rulers enforced religious uniformity (Louis XIV, James VI and I as head of the church), though Bodin favoured tolerance; inferred and split.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; dress codes were set by custom and sumptuary law rather than by any absolutist principle.

common-currency.rationale: Bodin lists the right to coin money among the marks of sovereignty, so a shared currency would surrender a sovereign prerogative.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Absolutist states were dynastic and territorial, not built on kinship of peoples; inferred from that dynastic basis.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Absolutism centralised law and administration under the crown and gave subjects no political voice, so self-governing minority institutions cut against it; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A modern minority question absent from the doctrine; no stance can be sourced.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: For Bossuet and James, kings rule by divine providence and divine right, so history is directed by God, not by economic change; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Crowns granted monopolies and chartered guilds as mercantilist policy; inferred that a ban on concentrations of economic power was not a goal.

no-bailouts.rationale: No documented stance; a paternal crown might rescue favoured firms, but the sources do not say.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Absolutism had no majority to defer to, and it opposed any body constraining the ruler; adherents have no clear stance on this modern question.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Public office was held by birth and royal favour, and women had no political role; inferred from the hierarchical order.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Mercantilism, which the sources tie to absolutism, aimed at a favourable balance of trade and exclusive colonial markets, though it did not seek full closure.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; mercantilist crowns regulated trade for state revenue, not for labor or environmental standards, so this is inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; loyalty was framed as duty to God and king, but no doctrine about work incentives exists.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Bodin forbids resistance to a sovereign even a cruel one, and Bossuet treats rebellion as sacrilege.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary monarchy and the privileges of estates were the foundation of the order absolutism defended.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from absolutist state-building, which tied subjects to the crown and the monarch's own realm.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from absolutist colonial expansion and the view that Christian monarchs could govern other peoples.

patriotic-education.rationale: Bossuet teaches that subjects owe the king obedience and loyalty as a religious duty, which schooling would reinforce.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Early modern absolutism did not address racial preferences, so no stance follows from its principles.

public-money-creation.rationale: Bodin counts the power to coin money among the sovereign's marks, so money creation belongs to the crown.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Absolutist mercantilism had no theory of capitalist crisis or collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from dynastic and mercantilist expansion, which sought influence over territories once held by the crown.

delink-world-market.rationale: Mercantilist absolutism favored protecting national economies and managing trade for the state's benefit.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Absolutism had no theory of global exploitation or labor aristocracy.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Bodin makes the sovereign supreme over subjects' conduct and property, so private owners would not hold an unlimited right to refuse service.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: James and Bodin hold the ruler is above positive law, so a charter that binds the sovereign is rejected.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Absolutists held that sovereign acts bind, but also that the sovereign may revise past agreements; inferred, since treaty voidness is anachronistic.

elective-rulers.rationale: Absolute monarchy rests on hereditary kingship, not election; Bossuet and James I defend succession by birth.

minority-veto.rationale: Bodin's indivisible sovereignty and the divine-right writers hold that the king's decisions bind all subjects without need of consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Bodin and Bossuet allow no lawful resistance; the ruler is accountable to God, not subjects, though Bodin keeps the ruler bound by natural and divine law.

parliament-supreme.rationale: James I holds that the king is author of law and that parliament is subordinate; Bodin makes the sovereign the lawmaker.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Absolutist writers do not address animals; inferred only from the Christian tradition, with adherents split.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the era's Christian view of animals as given to man for use, with kindness encouraged.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Bossuet and James I describe the king as paternal and bound to the welfare of subjects, with duty running down from the privileged; inferred for the wealthy in general.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Absolutist writers treat subjects' duty as obedience and loyal service, not political participation, but not a demand for withdrawal; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Mass media did not exist; the court did manage public culture and religion, but the statement is anachronistic.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources stress sacred authority and standing armies rather than a theory of cultural consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the absolutist mercantilist state, which favoured national wealth; dependency theory is anachronistic.

native-born-offices.rationale: Absolutist states favoured the king's own subjects in office, though they also hired foreign nobles and ministers; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Statement is anachronistic and addresses communist parties; absolutism has no doctrine on it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Mercantilist absolutism sought national self-sufficiency and bullion, inferred as favouring own resources; aid is anachronistic.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Absolutist monarchs fought wars to recover or extend territory and dynastic claims; inferred from the practice described in the overview.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from absolutism's hereditary rule by the monarch and its colonial-era practice; pre-colonial leadership is anachronistic.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism as a constitutional value implies democratic constitutionalism, which absolutism rejects.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; absolutists would condemn tyranny but not in these terms.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic; absolutism has no position on the American Civil War.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from absolutism's reverence for tradition and royal symbols, but monuments are a modern controversy.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: absolutism held the sovereign bound by divine and natural law, not by foreign institutions, so each realm has its own government.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Absolutism relied on a standing army loyal to the king, but placed it under royal command, not as an independent guardian; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Absolutist society was hierarchical and patriarchal; inferred, since the statement is anachronistic.

filial-duty.rationale: Bossuet grounds royal authority in paternal authority and the commandment to honour parents, so lifelong filial duty fits the paternalist order.

office-by-exam.rationale: Offices were granted by the crown, patronage and sale rather than examination; inferred from the court-centred bureaucracy the sources describe.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from absolutist mercantilism, which put trade and strategic industry under state direction for the crown's power.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic and Protestant churches' teaching on marriage, which absolutist monarchies upheld in law; divorce at will was unthinkable.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Sovereignty is indivisible and the king answers only to God, so binding or removing him by his subjects is rejected outright.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources give no basis for a view on private pension accounts versus state schemes.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Absolutist monarchies kept private, noble and church landholding under the crown; inferred, since the sources do not discuss communal tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The king makes law and the parliament is subordinate to him, so he needs no parliamentary approval to spend, though Bodin held he should not tax arbitrarily.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the centralisation of law and administration under absolutism, which favoured one language of state.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from mercantilist protection of the realm's wealth and the crown's concern for control of its territory.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Absolutist society was a hierarchy of orders with unequal legal status, so equal-outcome tests have no place; inferred from that structure.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Mercantilism and court display encouraged luxury production while moralists criticised excess; no settled doctrine, inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Dynastic rulers of the period routinely funded rebels and rival claimants abroad as an instrument of state power; inferred from their foreign policy.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the claim of sovereign power to enforce the dynastic and religious order; the sources do not address alliances.

missingStatements.text: A ruler is not bound by the positive laws that he or his predecessors made.
missingStatements.rationale: Bodin defines the absolute sovereign as free from civil law while bound by natural and divine law, and James calls kings the makers of the laws.

missingStatements.text: Subjects may never lawfully take up arms against a lawful ruler, even a cruel one.
missingStatements.rationale: Bodin forbids killing an absolute sovereign even if cruel and Bossuet treats attacks on the king as sacrilege.

notes: Enlightened absolutism (see its own profile) would differ on religion, serfdom and reason. Historians such as Mettam doubt the real power of absolutist monarchs, but the profile follows the doctrine.
